html:
The Ikpeng, also called Txikão, are a Carib-speaking Indigenous people who now live in the Xingu Indigenous Park in Mato Grosso, Brazil.

They lived further west, on tributaries of the Xingu, and were long at war with the peoples of the Upper Xingu such as the Kamaiurá. After first contact in 1964, flu and other diseases killed many of them. In 1967 the Villas-Bôas brothers moved the survivors into the park, where their numbers fell to about 50 in 1969. They have since recovered, to 459 people in 2010, and have worked to reclaim part of their old lands on the Jatobá River.
sum: The Ikpeng, also called Txikão, are a Carib-speaking Indigenous people who now live in the Xingu Indigenous Park in Mato Grosso, Brazil.
